title: LIVE SURFACE PRESSURE
source_name: NOAA/NCEP HRRR 3 km MSLMA mean sea-level pressure analysis (hourly cycles)
variable: MSLMA mean sea level, analysis step (filed Pa / 100 = hPa, the only conversion)
coverage: Basin rectangle lon -93..-73.5, lat 40.5..49.5 (all Great Lakes + land). No shoreline cut: full rectangle stays visible.
center_note: Average everyday pressure 1013.25 hPa sits in the MIDDLE of the gradient (yellow). Lower than average runs dark-blue->green to the left; higher than average runs orange->dark-purple to the right.
what: Hourly HRRR sea-level pressure analysis over the Great Lakes basin in hPa. The everyday average (1013.25 hPa) is the middle color so lows and highs read as departures from normal at a glance.
why_extreme: Deep storm lows (<990) and strong highs (>1032) compress into the endpoint purples; ordinary near-average weather owns most of the color resolution.
